sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐形。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: On July 10, 2015, a police officer in Prairie View, Texas, pulled over a 28-year-old black woman named Sandra Bland.
sentences.zh: 2015年7月10日，得克萨斯州草原景观市的一名警察拦下了一名28岁的黑人女性桑德拉·布兰德。

sentences.en: And she was pulled over for turning without signaling, which is a common infraction that police use to stop people in their cars today.
sentences.zh: 她因转弯不打转向灯而被拦下，这是如今警察用来拦截车主的常见违章行为。

sentences.en: This is Sarah Sayo, professor at Columbia Law School.
sentences.zh: 这位是哥伦比亚法学院教授莎拉·萨约。

sentences.en: And the traffic stop quickly turned hostile.
sentences.zh: 而这场交通拦截很快变得充满敌意。

sentences.en: There was confrontation between the officer about her smoking in her car, and the officer got upset.
sentences.zh: 警察和她之间就她在车里抽烟一事发生了冲突，警察为此很不高兴。

sentences.en: Many of you have probably seen the footage of this arreSt. It is very disturbing.
sentences.zh: 你们中的很多人可能都看过这段逮捕录像。它非常令人不安。

sentences.en: The officer drags Bland out of the car and threatens her with a taser.
sentences.zh: 警察将布兰德从车里拖出来，并用电击枪威胁她。

sentences.en: He then arrests her and takes her to jail, where she tragically dies three days later.
sentences.zh: 随后他逮捕了她并将她带到监狱，三天后她在那里不幸身亡。

sentences.en: Bland's death was ruled a suicide, but her treatment at the hands of the police sparked outrage across the country.
sentences.zh: 布兰德的死被裁定为自杀，但她在警察手中的遭遇在全国引发了愤怒。

sentences.en: About a year later, the magazine The Nation published an article trying to analyze everything that went wrong leading up to her arreSt.
sentences.zh: 大约一年后，《国家》杂志发表了一篇文章，试图剖析导致她被捕前发生的一切问题。

sentences.en: They focused not just on the incident itself, but her entire life's history, her experiences with unemployment, poverty, and mental illness.
sentences.zh: 他们的关注点不仅在于事件本身，还在于她整个人生经历、她遭遇失业、贫困以及精神疾病的经历。

sentences.en: And when I read the article in The Nation about Sandra Bland's biography,
sentences.zh: 当我读到《国家》杂志关于桑德拉·布兰德生平的文章时，

sentences.en: one thing that stood out to me was every moment in her life where she experienced a setback happened in the context of her car,
sentences.zh: 有一件事让我感触很深，那就是她人生中每一次遭遇挫折的时刻，都发生在汽车的语境下，

sentences.en: where the police stopped her in her car for a traffic violation, a parking violation that she couldn't afford to pay.
sentences.zh: 当时警察在车里拦下她，是因为她有交通违章行为，或者是交不起的停车违章。

sentences.en: And so she sat out in jail because the police found marijuana in her car that she was using to self-medicate her mental health issues.
sentences.zh: 因此她只能在监狱里苦等，因为警察在她的车里发现了她用来自我治疗心理健康问题的古柯碱。

sentences.en: And so for me, I saw the car as this important character in itself in the systematic ways that Black Americans today, Black people today in America,
sentences.zh: 因此对我而言，我认为汽车本身就是今天美国系统性歧视黑人、今天美国的黑人，

sentences.en: are discriminated against, treated unequally in the justice system.
sentences.zh: 在司法系统中遭到不平等对待这一现象中一个重要的角色。

sentences.en: Sarah Sayo's new book is called Policing the Open Road, How Cars Transformed American Freedom.
sentences.zh: 莎拉·萨约的新书名为《巡视开阔道路：汽车如何重塑美国自由》。

sentences.en: And it's basically a historical analysis of how we got into this situation,
sentences.zh: 这基本上是对我们如何陷入这种局面的历史分析，

sentences.en: where police have so much power over people in their cars,
sentences.zh: 在那种局面下，警察对车内民众拥有如此巨大的权力，

sentences.en: where black and brown people are stopped and searched disproportionately,
sentences.zh: 黑人和棕色人种被不成比例地拦下并搜查，

sentences.en: and where a minor traffic violation, like failing to use a turn signal, can have deadly consequences.
sentences.zh: 而像未能打转向灯这样微小的交通违章，也可能导致致命的后果。

sentences.en: Sayo brilliantly connects the history of modern policing
sentences.zh: 萨约精妙地将现代警务的历史

sentences.en: with the history of the car.
sentences.zh: 与汽车的历史联系在了一起。

sentences.en: It's a riveting read and an important book for this moment,
sentences.zh: 这是一本引人入胜且对当下而言极其重要的书，

sentences.en: and I wanted to talk with Professor Sayo about it.
sentences.zh: 我想就此与萨约教授聊聊。

sentences.en: We started 100 years ago, at the dawn of the automotive age.
sentences.zh: 我们从100年前汽车时代的曙光开始讲起。

sentences.en: All of a sudden, there were hundreds and thousands of mass-produced cars on streets that were not meant for them.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，原本并不为此设计的街道上涌现出了成百上千辆大规模生产的汽车。

sentences.en: These streets were intended for pedestrians,
sentences.zh: 这些街道原本是为行人准备的，

sentences.en: children played in the streets,
sentences.zh: 孩子们在街上玩耍，

sentences.en: trolleys,
sentences.zh: 还有有轨电车，

sentences.en: a few horse-drawn carriages that could be afforded by the wealthy,
sentences.zh: 以及少数富人才能买得起的马车，

sentences.en: and to have suddenly have dozens and then hundreds and then thousands of cars on these streets
sentences.zh: 而突然之间街道上出现了几十辆、上百辆甚至上千辆汽车，

sentences.en: created chaos and created traffic.
sentences.zh: 这造成了混乱和交通拥堵。

sentences.en: So what did we do to respond to the safety issues
sentences.zh: 那么，我们如何应对安全问题呢？

sentences.en: that were the result of thousands of cars being thrown onto city streets that were not designed for cars?
sentences.zh: 这些安全问题正是成千上万辆汽车涌入并非为汽车设计的城市街道所导致的？

sentences.en: So we have to think back to a time before the rules of the road became standardized.
sentences.zh: 所以我们必须回想一下道路规则尚未标准化之前的那个时期。

sentences.en: There were no moral sense of telling us what are the norms of driving on the road, right?
sentences.zh: 当时还没有道德意识来告诉我们道路上驾驶的规范是什么，对吧？

sentences.en: And so local governments, when they addressed the traffic problem,
sentences.zh: 因此，地方政府在解决交通问题时，

sentences.en: had to pass a lot of laws setting forth norms so that everybody drove uniformly
sentences.zh: 不得不通过大量法律来制定规范，以便每个人都能统一驾驶，

sentences.en: because that was the best way to achieve safety on the road.
sentences.zh: 因为那是实现道路安全的最佳方式。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And there were so many of these new laws that it ended up being pretty confusing,
sentences.zh: 而且这类新法律实在太多，以至于最后相当令人困惑，

sentences.en: especially because they varied from state to state and county to county.
sentences.zh: 特别是由于它们因州而异、因县而异。

sentences.en: And so local governments needed to really work to get people to understand these laws and to follow them.
sentences.zh: 因此，地方政府需要真正努力让人们理解这些法律并遵守它们。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And they tried a mix of old ways of responding to social problems
sentences.zh: 他们尝试将应对社会问题的旧方法结合起来，

sentences.en: while searching for new solutions because the car was an innovation that they had not experienced before.
sentences.zh: 同时寻找新的解决方案，因为汽车是他们从未经历过的创新。

sentences.en: And so some of the old ways that they tried to respond was through private, voluntary actions.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们尝试应对的一些旧方法是通过民间的、自愿的行动。

sentences.en: Ministers in churches gave sermons on Safety Sunday, exhorting their congregants to obey traffic laws.
sentences.zh: 教堂的牧师在安全主日上发表布道，告诫他们的会众遵守交通法规。

sentences.en: They also had school boys, preferably Boy Scouts, direct traffic near schools.
sentences.zh: 他们还让学童，最好是童子军，在学校附近指挥交通。

sentences.en: Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿特区

sentences.en: even had women volunteer to manage traffic and report traffic violations.
sentences.zh: 甚至让女性志愿者来管理交通并报告交通违章行为。

sentences.en: And so some of the old ways of governing relied on private citizens and volunteers
sentences.zh: 因此，一些旧的治理方式依赖于普通公民和志愿者

sentences.en: to try to maintain order on the streets.
sentences.zh: 来试图维持街道上的秩序。

sentences.en: But these were ineffective.
sentences.zh: 但这些都是无效的。

sentences.en: And they were ineffective because average citizens who owned and drove cars refused to obey traffic laws.
sentences.zh: 它们之所以无效，是因为拥有并驾驶汽车的普通公民拒绝遵守交通法规。

sentences.en: They kept breaking them.
sentences.zh: 他们一直在违章。

sentences.en: And one of the most common laws that they broke were speeding limits,
sentences.zh: 他们触犯的最常见法律之一就是超速限制，

sentences.en: which was the number one contributing factor to accidents.
sentences.zh: 这是导致事故的首要因素。

sentences.en: And so they realized relying on old ways of governing people, relying on their sense of honor to obey the laws wouldn't work.
sentences.zh: 因此他们意识到，依赖管理人们的旧方式、依赖他们的荣誉感来遵守法律是行不通的。

sentences.en: And so they started shifting towards police law enforcement.
sentences.zh: 于是他们开始转向警察执法。

sentences.en: And the police at this time, they were not what we think of today.
sentences.zh: 当时的警察并不是我们今天所想的那样。

sentences.en: Like police forces were really small.
sentences.zh: 比如警察队伍非常小。

sentences.en: Officers weren't really trained for the job.
sentences.zh: 警员并没有真正接受过这份工作的培训。

sentences.en: They were often like plainclothes and maybe they had a little 10-star, almost like a night watchman or something.
sentences.zh: 他们通常穿着便服，可能还有一个小十角星徽章，几乎就像守夜人一样。

sentences.en: And they weren't really in the business of policing, you know, the kind of upper middle class,
sentences.zh: 他们其实并不从事那种治安维护工作，你知道的，也就是针对中产阶级上层、

sentences.en: otherwise law-abiding people who were all of a sudden driving around in cars and breaking all these new traffic laws.
sentences.zh: 原本遵纪守法、却突然开始开车并违反所有这些新交通法规的人们。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And so what local governments throughout the country realized was that trying to enforce the law against normally law-abiding citizens,
sentences.zh: 因此，全国各地的地方政府意识到，试图针对通常遵纪守法的公民、

sentences.en: the respectable members of society, required somebody with more authority.
sentences.zh: 社会受人尊敬的成员执法，需要更有权威的人。

sentences.en: It required somebody with good judgment.
sentences.zh: 这需要一个有良好判断力的人。

sentences.en: It required somebody who knew the laws, right, to stand head-to-head and toe-to-toe with the respectable members of society,
sentences.zh: 这需要一个懂法律的人，对吧，能够与社会上受人尊敬的成员针锋相对、平起平坐，

sentences.en: even the wealthy ones who drove their cars too faSt.
sentences.zh: 甚至是那些开车开得太快的富人。

sentences.en: And what they realized is they needed police officers to be professionals.
sentences.zh: 他们意识到，他们需要警察成为专业人士。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so we see, because of the automobile, a shift to professionalize and modernize police departments
sentences.zh: 因此，由于汽车的出现，我们看到警察部门转向专业化和现代化，

sentences.en: who couldn't be bribed, who were smart enough to learn all the laws, who were tall enough.
sentences.zh: 他们不会被贿赂，足够聪明能学会所有法律，个子也足够高。

sentences.en: There was actually a height requirement so that they could stand above the cars
sentences.zh: 当时实际上有身高要求，这样他们才能站在汽车上方，

sentences.en: and people could see their directions managing traffic.
sentences.zh: 人们才能看到他们指挥交通的手势。

sentences.en: And so we see how the police profession itself become more specialized and exclusive out of necessity
sentences.zh: 因此，我们看到警察职业本身由于纪律约束驾驶员的需求，

sentences.en: because of the need to discipline drivers.
sentences.zh: 出于必要变得更加专业化和排他性。

sentences.en: So was the decision to involve the police in all this, like, controversial?
sentences.zh: 那么，让警察介入这一切的决定，是不是很有争议？

sentences.en: I mean, today we take it for granted that police enforce traffic laws,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，今天我们认为警察执行交通法是理所当然的，

sentences.en: but was there any debate about that at the time?
sentences.zh: 但在当时对此有什么争论吗？

sentences.en: There was debate.
sentences.zh: 确实有争论。

sentences.en: There was a group of reforming police chiefs who wanted to modernize and professionalize the police.
sentences.zh: 有一群力求改革的警察局长，他们想要将警察现代化和专业化。

sentences.en: And the person at the forefront of that movement was a police chief named August Wilmer.
sentences.zh: 而该运动的带头人是一位名叫奥古斯特·沃尔默的警察局长。

sentences.en: He was a police chief of Berkeley, California from 1905 to 1932.
sentences.zh: 他在1905年至1932年担任加利福尼亚州伯克利市的警察局长。

sentences.en: And a lot of police scholars today call him the father of modern policing in America.
sentences.zh: 如今许多警务学者称他为美国现代警务之父。

sentences.en: And he firmly believed that the police should not enforce traffic.
sentences.zh: 他坚信警察不应该执行交通执法。

sentences.en: He also believed that the police should not enforce vice laws because the police as professionals were crime fighters
sentences.zh: 他还认为警察不应该执行风化法，因为作为专业人士的警察是犯罪打击者，

sentences.en: and they should devote their time to fighting and investigating crime,
sentences.zh: 他们应该将时间奉献给打击和调查犯罪，

sentences.en: not enforcing traffic laws or vice laws like prostitution or anti-liquor laws.
sentences.zh: 而不是执行交通法或诸如卖淫或禁酒令等风化法。

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错。

sentences.en: Like, he didn't see those as serious crimes worthy of the police's attention.
sentences.zh: 就像他并不认为那些是值得警察关注的严重犯罪一样。

sentences.en: Like, it was more of an administrative task than, you know, professional police work.
sentences.zh: 这更像是一项行政任务，而不是你知道的专业警察工作。

sentences.en: Yeah, and I think the other thing is that traffic quickly came to consume much of the police's time.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为另一件事是，交通很快就占据了警察的大部分时间。

sentences.en: It became a large part of their duties.
sentences.zh: 这成为了他们职责很大的一部分。

sentences.en: And for the police to enforce the letter of the law against these ordinarily law-abiding citizens
sentences.zh: 事实证明，要让警察对这些原本遵纪守法的公民严格执行法律的字面规定

sentences.en: proved to be a huge headache because nobody liked being enforced.
sentences.zh: 是一件极其令人头疼的事，因为没有人喜欢被执法。

sentences.en: Nobody liked to be ticketed.
sentences.zh: 没有人喜欢收到罚单。

sentences.en: Nobody liked to be arrested for a traffic violation.
sentences.zh: 没有人喜欢因交通违章而被捕。

sentences.en: And so he, what Vollmer saw was that this, what he called the respectable citizenry,
sentences.zh: 因此沃尔默看到，他所谓的受人尊敬的市民们

sentences.en: started turning against the police.
sentences.zh: 开始对抗警察。

sentences.en: And he hated that because police as professionals were owed respect, not disdain.
sentences.zh: 他痛恨这一点，因为作为专业人士的警察应该得到尊重，而不是蔑视。

sentences.en: And so what he realized to manage this kind of public relations rule of law problem
sentences.zh: 因此，为了管理这种公共关系和法治问题，他意识到

sentences.en: was to advise his officers actually exercise your judgment and discretion.
sentences.zh: 应该建议他的警官们实际行使你们的判断力和自由裁量权。

sentences.en: And let's not enforce the law to the letter.
sentences.zh: 我们不要刻板地执行法律。

sentences.en: Let's mitigate the harshness of the law.
sentences.zh: 让我们减轻法律的严厉性。

sentences.en: Even if the law says to arrest somebody for a traffic violation, let's just let them go
sentences.zh: 即使法律规定因交通违章逮捕某人，我们也干脆放他们走，

sentences.en: with the warning.
sentences.zh: 给个警告就行。

sentences.en: It's better to manage our relations with the citizenry rather than to antagonize and alienate
sentences.zh: 与其激怒和疏远市民，不如处理好我们与市民的关系。

sentences.en: them.
sentences.zh: 他们。

sentences.en: So he definitely saw the challenges of traffic law enforcement that he did not like at all.
sentences.zh: 因此他确实看到了交通执法的挑战，而这是他非常讨厌的。

sentences.en: Even though his opposition didn't end up mattering that much.
sentences.zh: 尽管他的反对最终并没有那么重要。

sentences.en: It was like, this is an interesting irony that you present in the book is that cars ended
sentences.zh: 这就好像，你在书中提出了一个有趣的讽刺，那就是汽车最终

sentences.en: up helping Vollmer achieve his goals and having a more modern professional police force because
sentences.zh: 帮助沃尔默实现了他的目标，拥有了一支更加现代化的专业警察队伍，因为

sentences.en: so many people were breaking traffic laws that meant they had to have more police, more police
sentences.zh: 有太多人违反交通法，这意味着他们必须有更多的警察，更多的警官

sentences.en: officers on the road, and they needed their own patrol cars and all the traffic tickets
sentences.zh: 在路上巡逻，他们需要自己的巡逻车，而且所有的交通罚单

sentences.en: help pay for all of it.
sentences.zh: 都有助于支付这一切的费用。

sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.zh: 而他并非完全预料到、但却相当快发生的事情是，美国

sentences.zh: 社会变成了一个汽车社会。

sentences.zh: 因此无论如何，很多犯罪活动本就发生在道路上的汽车里。

sentences.zh: 因此很早以前，地方和州政府官员就意识到打击犯罪

sentences.zh: 和刑事调查，其中很大一部分都发生在路上。

sentences.zh: 因此我们看到交通执法、刑法执法

sentences.zh: 和风化执法这几项职责融合在了一起。

sentences.zh: 而汽车是运输私酒的最佳途径之一。

sentences.zh: 人们免受不当搜查和扣押。

sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，就像我们大家可能从看电视中了解到的那样，警察需要

sentences.zh: 你的汽车。

sentences.zh: 因此，大麻气味已经成为警察在全部情况中为了支持合理根据而普遍添加的借口。

sentences.en: It really comes down to whether the judge believes the police officer that he or she smelled marijuana in the car.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: There's nothing else that a person can do to disprove that fact other than to challenge the credibility of the officer.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，比较神奇的一点是，你知道的，我是一个四十多岁的白人男性。

sentences.en: And so this odor of marijuana has become this really common thing that officers will add to their account
sentences.zh: 我负担得起请好律师的费用。

sentences.en: in the totality of the circumstances to support probable cause.
sentences.zh: 如果一个警察开着车跟在我的车后面，而我自认为表现得很正常

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 并且遵守规则，我还是会感到害怕。

sentences.en: I mean, one of the things that's pretty amazing is that, you know, I'm, you know, a white man in his 40s.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，就像我觉得自己做错了什么，或者觉得我有可能会做错什么一样。

sentences.en: I can afford to hire a good lawyer.
sentences.zh: 我甚至无法想象，对于处境不如我的人、对于黑人男性而言，风险高得多时，那会是怎样的感受。

sentences.en: And if a police officer pulls behind me in my car while I'm just, what I think of is behaving normally
sentences.zh: 我们为什么接受了这一切？

sentences.en: and adhering to the rules, I get scared.
sentences.zh: 我们为什么会接受这样一种动态，即一个普通警察对车里的个人拥有如此巨大的权力？

sentences.en: You know, like I think I've done something wrong or I think there's the potential that I will do something wrong.
sentences.zh: 我想我们已经接受了。

sentences.en: And I can't even imagine what that is like for someone not in my situation, for a black man where the risk is so much higher.
sentences.zh: 我认为法官之所以接受它，是因为汽车带来的种种危险。

sentences.en: Why have we accepted this?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们要接受这个？

sentences.en: Like why have we accepted this dynamic where an individual police officer has so much power over a person in their car?
sentences.zh: 比如，为什么我们要接受这种动态，即单个警官对车里的人拥有如此大的权力？

sentences.en: I think we accept it.
sentences.zh: 我想我们接受了它。

sentences.en: And I think the reason why judges have accepted it is because of the dangers of cars.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为法官之所以接受它，是因为汽车带来的危险。

sentences.en: Cars are really dangerous.
sentences.zh: 汽车真的很危险。

sentences.en: Road safety is a big issue.
sentences.zh: 道路安全是一个大问题。

sentences.en: I am scared of drunk drivers.
sentences.zh: 我害怕酒驾司机。

sentences.en: They're a huge problem on the road, right?
sentences.zh: 他们在路上是个巨大的问题，对吧？

sentences.en: I want to be protected by the state.
sentences.zh: 我希望得到国家的保护。

sentences.en: That is a legitimate function of the government.
sentences.zh: 这是政府合法的职能。

sentences.en: It's just that because we've delegated that task to the police, that also handles criminal enforcement.
sentences.zh: 只是因为我们把这项任务委派给了警察，而警察还要负责刑事执法。

sentences.en: That's caused so much of the problems we see today.
sentences.zh: 这引发了我们今天看到的这么多问题。

sentences.en: And so I think part of the answer to your question of why haven't we questioned the police enforcement of traffic laws
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得，对于你刚才问的“为什么我们没有质疑过警察对交通法规的执法”这个问题，部分答案在于

sentences.en: is I think goes back to traffic safety is a huge deal.
sentences.zh: 我认为归根结底是因为交通安全是一件大事。

sentences.en: But we can question whether the police are the right institution to handle that or not.
sentences.zh: 但我们可以质疑警察是否是处理这件事的合适机构。

sentences.en: Coming up after the break, we're going to take a look at a city that is doing just that,
sentences.zh: 休息之后，我们将带大家了解一个正在这样做的城市，

sentences.en: separating traffic enforcement from its police department.
sentences.zh: 他们将交通执法与警察局剥离。

sentences.en: After this.
sentences.zh: 广告之后继续。

sentences.en: So the town I live in, Berkeley, California.
sentences.zh: 我住的城镇是加利福尼亚州的伯克利。

sentences.en: I live in Berkeley.
sentences.zh: 我住在伯克利。

sentences.en: The headquarters is in beautiful downtown Oakland, California.
sentences.zh: 总部位于美丽的加州奥克兰市中心。

sentences.en: But I live in Berkeley.
sentences.zh: 但我住在伯克利。

sentences.en: It was also the home of the police chief, August Vollmer, the so-called father of modern policing.
sentences.zh: 这里也是警察局长奥古斯特·沃尔默的故居，他被称为现代警察制度之父。

sentences.en: Actually, he lived like around the corner from my house.
sentences.zh: 其实，他就住在离我家拐角不远的地方。

sentences.en: But as Sarah Sayo talks about in her book, Vollmer was not a fan of the idea that police should be in charge of enforcing traffic laws.
sentences.zh: 但正如萨拉·萨约在她的书中所说，沃尔默并不赞成由警察来负责执行交通法规。

sentences.en: He did not consider rolling through a stop sign to be a crime worthy of the police's attention.
sentences.zh: 他认为开车滑行通过停车标志算不上什么需要警察关注的犯罪。

sentences.en: So a hundred years later, the city of Berkeley has made a decision that August Vollmer might have approved of.
sentences.zh: 因此，一百年后，伯克利市做出了一个奥古斯特·沃尔默可能会赞同的决定。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So in July of 2020, Berkeley City Council passed this big omnibus motion related to policing.
sentences.zh: 所以在2020年7月，伯克利市议会通过了一项关于警务的大型综合动议。

sentences.en: And one of the strategies in there had to do with traffic.
sentences.zh: 其中的一项策略就与交通有关。

sentences.en: That's producer Emmett Fitzgerald.
sentences.zh: 那是制作人埃米特·菲茨杰拉德。

sentences.en: Hello, Emmett.
sentences.zh: 你好，埃米特。

sentences.en: Hey.
sentences.zh: 嘿。

sentences.en: So explain what actually happened there.
sentences.zh: 那么，给我们讲讲那里到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: So the council is basically beginning the process of taking traffic enforcement out of the hands of its police department.
sentences.zh: 所以市议会基本上开始着手将交通执法权从警察局移交出去。

sentences.en: They voted to create a new body, the Department of Transportation, or BERC DOT, as they're calling it, which, you know,
sentences.zh: 他们投票决定创建一个新机构——交通局，或者他们所称的BERC DOT，你知道的，

sentences.en: in addition to doing all the things like traffic engineering and more structural stuff, would also administer the rules of the road.
sentences.zh: 除了负责交通工程和更多结构性工作之外，它还将管理道路规则。

sentences.en: And, you know, this is very much in the early stages, but that's the intention.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这还在非常初期的阶段，但这就是他们的意图。

sentences.en: That's like what they're setting out to do.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们着手要做的事情。

sentences.en: And one thing that I found so interesting was that the whole idea for this proposal was actually inspired in part by Sarah Sayo's book.
sentences.zh: 我发现非常有趣的一点是，这个提案的整个构想实际上部分受到了萨拉·萨约的书的启发。

sentences.en: We're influenced by Sarah Sayo's book because I think what it brought forward is this idea that it doesn't have to be this way.
sentences.zh: 我们受到了萨拉·萨约书的影响，因为我认为它带来了一种理念，即事情并非只能如此。

sentences.en: This is Barnali Ghosh.
sentences.zh: 这位是巴尔纳利·戈什。

sentences.en: She's a transportation advocate here in Berkeley.
sentences.zh: 她是伯克利的一位交通倡导者。

sentences.en: She's on the coordinating committee of a community organization called Walk Bike Berkeley and is the chair of the Berkeley Transportation Commission,
sentences.zh: 她是社区组织“步行骑行伯克利”协调委员会的成员，也是伯克利交通委员会的主席，

sentences.en: which is a body that advises Berkeley City Council on transportation issues.
sentences.zh: 该机构负责就交通问题向伯克利市议会提供建议。

sentences.en: And Ghosh says that one of her colleagues at Walk Bike Berkeley actually heard Sarah Sayo speak on another podcast, the Great War on Cars podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 戈什说，“步行骑行伯克利”的一位同事在另一个播客《伟大的汽车战争》中听到了萨拉·萨约的演讲。

sentences.en: Check it out.
sentences.zh: 去听听看吧。

sentences.en: And that got them interested in all this history, and particularly in August Vollmer.
sentences.zh: 这让他们对这段历史产生了兴趣，尤其是对奥古斯特·沃尔默。

sentences.en: You know, Vollmer, who is seen often as the father of modern policing, all kinds of issues with him.
sentences.zh: 你知道，沃尔默经常被视为现代警察制度之父，他身上有很多争议。

sentences.en: But even he, even the father of modern policing, didn't think that traffic enforcement should be part of the police department.
sentences.zh: 但即使是他，即使是现代警察制度之父，也认为交通执法不应该成为警察局的一部分。

sentences.en: And that's something we also learned from Sarah Sayo's book.
sentences.zh: 这也是我们从萨拉·萨约书中了解到的内容。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, I was totally riveted by that section and thought it was just kind of remarkable.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我完全被那一节吸引了，觉得这简直太了不起了。

sentences.en: Yeah, and that just got Ghosh and the folks at Walk Bike Berkeley and other community groups thinking, like, does it have to be this way?
sentences.zh: 对，这让戈什、“步行骑行伯克利”的成员以及其他社区团体开始思考：事情必须是这样的吗？

sentences.en: I think for a long time, we all took it for granted that, of course, police is going to do traffic enforcement.
sentences.zh: 我想很长一段时间以来，我们都理所当然地认为警察当然会负责交通执法。

sentences.en: But you actually think about it, the more we share this idea with people,
sentences.zh: 但你仔细想想，当我们把这个想法分享给越来越多的人时，

sentences.en: it becomes quite clear that you don't need armed police to ticket somebody who's might have stepped off the curb a few minutes before the light changed.
sentences.zh: 就会变得非常清楚：你并不需要全副武装的警察去给一个可能在绿灯变亮前几秒钟踏下马路牙子的人开罚单。

sentences.en: And, you know, Ghosh has been working on transit issues for a long time, you know, questions of safety and how we can redesign our cities to make them safer and rely less on cars.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，戈什长期以来一直致力于交通问题，你知道，包括安全问题以及我们如何重新设计城市以使其更安全、减少对汽车的依赖。

sentences.en: And she says that enforcement, you know, has always been a major obstacle to getting everyone in the community on board.
sentences.zh: 她说，执法一直是让社区所有人达成共识的主要障碍。

sentences.en: We do have a lot of anger against cars, which are dangerous.
sentences.zh: 我们对汽车确实有很多愤怒，因为它们很危险。

sentences.en: You know, we are upset when people park in the bike lane.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当有人把车停在自行车道上时，我们会感到沮丧。

sentences.en: And enforcement is seen as a tool to create safe streets.
sentences.zh: 执法被视为打造安全街道的一种工具。

sentences.en: But we as transportation advocates are really tired of using transportation safety as a way to stop people.
sentences.zh: 但我们作为交通倡导者，真的厌倦了把交通安全作为拦下人们的借口。

sentences.en: The folks in our community, especially black community members, were telling us we do not want more police in our neighborhoods so you can have safety.
sentences.zh: 我们社区的人，尤其是黑人社区成员，一直在告诉我们：我们不希望社区里有更多警察，以此来换取你们的安全。

sentences.en: So we were already beginning to think about what safety looks like from an inclusive perspective.
sentences.zh: 所以我们已经开始从包容的视角来思考安全是什么样的。

sentences.en: So not just not getting hit by a car, but also not being harassed by police when you're when you're out walking in the streets.
sentences.zh: 不仅是不被汽车撞到，还包括当你在街上行走时不会受到警察的骚扰。

sentences.en: Okay, so Berkeley has created this new Department of Transportation that theoretically will oversee traffic enforcement.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以伯克利创建了这个新的交通局，理论上它将监督交通执法。

sentences.en: But what is that like specifically?
sentences.zh: 但这具体是怎样的呢？

sentences.en: Like, like, who will be the person who, like, stops someone to give them a speeding ticket?
sentences.zh: 比如，谁会是那个拦下某人并给他开超速罚单的人呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, so I asked Bernali Ghosh about this.
sentences.zh: 对，所以我问了巴尔纳利·戈什关于这方面的问题。

sentences.en: And again, it's like the very, very early stages of this.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，这还处于非常非常早期的阶段。

sentences.en: And so there is no concrete answer to that.
sentences.zh: 所以目前还没有具体的答案。

sentences.en: But she gave me the analogy of a building inspector.
sentences.zh: 但她给了我一个建筑检查员的类比。

sentences.en: So if a building inspector is coming in to check if you are up to code, they're not carrying a gun to enter your house, you know, expecting that they might find drugs.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果一个建筑检查员来检查你的建筑是否符合规范，他们进你家门时是不会带着枪的，也不会指望能搜出毒品。

sentences.en: So why is it okay then to use a violation of traffic safety to escalate to something more than that?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么利用违反交通安全来升级为更严重的事情就是可以接受的呢？

sentences.en: That's a good metaphor.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的隐喻。

sentences.en: So so so something like the building inspector, but for traffic is the thing.
sentences.zh: 所以，就是像建筑检查员那样，不过对象是交通，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think something kind of like that, an unarmed person who is an expert in traffic and transportation issues.
sentences.zh: 对，我想差不多就是这样，一个手无寸铁、精通交通和运输问题的人。

sentences.en: And and crucially, and this was an interesting part of the conversation.
sentences.zh: 而且至关重要的一点——这也是谈话中很有趣的部分。

sentences.en: Crucially, Ghosh is a person that could also, you know, be a part of the effort to to engineer and make our streets better.
sentences.zh: 至关重要的是，戈什这样的人也可以参与到设计和改善我们街道的工作中来。

sentences.en: So that person could use, you know, in responding to a specific incident, they're also able to help provide data on what went wrong from the perspective of urban design.
sentences.zh: 因此，这个人不仅能在应对特定事件时发挥作用，还能从城市设计的角度提供有关哪里出错了的数据。

sentences.en: They will be able to report back to the to work to the Department of Transportation on what are some of the infrastructural issues that might be causing people to are they not able to see the stop sign?
sentences.zh: 他们将能够向交通局汇报，看看到底是什么基础设施问题导致了人们的问题——比如是不是看不清停车标志？

sentences.en: Is there a tree branch blocking it?
sentences.zh: 是不是有树枝挡住了？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So we hope that it can be somebody who who is thinking whose main priority is traffic safety, not looking for crime.
sentences.zh: 所以我们希望这个人是一位优先考虑交通安全、而不是去抓捕犯罪的人。

sentences.en: And Ghosh really emphasized this a lot in our conversation, that the traffic enforcement should always be done in conjunction with better design and engineering.
sentences.zh: 戈什在我们的谈话中多次强调这一点，交通执法应始终与更好的设计和工程相结合。

sentences.en: So anytime you have a violation, you ask, like, is there something about the way that these streets are designed that could have prevented this?
sentences.zh: 因此，每当发生违规事件时，你都要问：这些街道的设计方式中，是否有某种因素本可以防止这种情况的发生？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So it's like instead of the way it is right now, where policing is totally distinct from planning and engineering and design, it's just a layer added on top of all that stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以它不同于现在这种警务工作与规划、工程和设计完全脱节的状态，后者只是在所有这些事情之上额外加的一层。

sentences.en: And they do not talk to each other at all.
sentences.zh: 而且他们根本不交流。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And Ghosh is like very bullish on this, that, you know,
sentences.zh: 戈什对此非常乐观，她认为，

sentences.en: so many traffic problems are really design problems and that we can reduce the amount of enforcement that is needed really dramatically.
sentences.zh: 许多交通问题本质上都是设计问题，只要这些不同的机构共同合作、共享数据并设计出真正的安全街道，

sentences.en: If these different agencies work together and share data and design streets that are safe streets.
sentences.zh: 我们就能极其显著地减少所需的执法力度。

sentences.en: So in our interview, I asked Sarah Sayo about this new policy in Berkeley,
sentences.zh: 所以在我们的采访中，我问了萨拉·萨约关于伯克利这项新政策的看法，

sentences.en: and she said that she thinks it's really exciting and that it's a great way to reduce bad interactions between the public and the police because traffic stops are the number one way that people come into contact with law enforcement.
sentences.zh: 她说她觉得这非常令人兴奋，这是减少公众与警察之间不良互动的好方法，因为交通拦截是人们与执法部门接触的最主要途径。

sentences.en: And I think this makes a lot of sense.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这很有道理。

sentences.en: One is that the police today are trained in what is called the warrior mentality because they are trained to deal with criminal suspects, to investigate crime,
sentences.zh: 一方面，今天的警察接受的是所谓的“战士心态”训练，因为他们受训是为了处理犯罪嫌疑人、调查犯罪、

sentences.en: to pursue criminal investigations.
sentences.zh: 进行刑事调查。

sentences.en: They tend to see a lot of their encounters in that warrior mentality,
sentences.zh: 他们往往会用这种战士心态来看待自己的许多遭遇，

sentences.en: which is not necessarily appropriate to traffic law enforcement when it's supposed to be a routine administrative task.
sentences.zh: 当交通执法本应是一项例行的行政任务时，这种心态不一定合适。

sentences.en: I think that the history that I tell in my book points to some difficulties with this proposal or some challenges to this proposal that have to be addressed.
sentences.zh: 我认为我在书中讲述的历史指出了这一提案的一些困难或挑战，这些是必须解决的。

sentences.en: And what are some of those logistical difficulties?
sentences.zh: 那么其中一些后勤方面的困难是什么呢？

sentences.en: The argument that I make in my book is that the police became professionalized, they became modernized,
sentences.zh: 我在书中提出的论点是，警察之所以走向专业化、现代化，

sentences.en: they gained a lot of discretionary power because of the challenges of enforcing traffic laws on the general public.
sentences.zh: 并且获得了大量自由裁量权，正是因为在广大公众中执行交通法规带来了种种挑战。

sentences.en: I saw this history repeat itself in the 1990s New York City experiment with meter maids where New York City has these traffic agents that are not police officers and they're informally called meter maids.
sentences.zh: 我在20世纪90年代纽约市关于停车管理员的试验中看到了这段历史重演，当时纽约市有一些交通协管员，他们不是警察，非正式地被称为“抄表员”。

sentences.en: And they issue citations for low-level offenses, mostly parking violations, and they realized the same thing that traffic cops in the 1920s and 30s realized.
sentences.zh: 他们对低级别违规行为（主要是违章停车）开具罚单，他们意识到了20至30年代的交通警察所意识到的同一件事。

sentences.en: Enforcing traffic laws on the general public is a really hard task.
sentences.zh: 在广大公众中执行交通法规是一项非常艰巨的任务。

sentences.en: And they got a lot of abuse, they were actually assaulted.
sentences.zh: 他们遭到了很多辱骂，甚至遭到了人身攻击。

sentences.en: And so what they wanted, what they lobbied for was to have the status and the authority of police officers because they thought if I have the power of a police officer,
sentences.zh: 因此，他们想要并游说争取的是警察的身份和权威，因为他们觉得如果我有警察的权力，

sentences.en: then the public won't abuse me or assault me when I'm directing traffic.
sentences.zh: 我在指挥交通时，公众就不会辱骂我或攻击我。

sentences.en: And so basically in New York City, they did everything they could to make meter maids more like police officers in the end.
sentences.zh: 所以在纽约市，他们最终竭尽全力让这些停车管理员变得更像警察。

sentences.en: So they gave them blue uniforms and they gave them more power and they kind of reinvented the police.
sentences.zh: 于是他们给他们穿上蓝色制服，赋予他们更大的权力，某种程度上算是重新发明了警察。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And then you end up in a situation that looks an awful lot like the one you were trying to get away from.
sentences.zh: 然后你最终会陷入一种与你当初极力想要摆脱的状况非常相似的境地。

sentences.en: So Sarah says that if Berkeley is going to create this new class of traffic enforcer,
sentences.zh: 所以萨拉说，如果伯克利要创建这种新型的交通执法人员，

sentences.en: the city is really going to have to work hard on public education and buy-in so that that type of power and force is not required in this new enforcement body.
sentences.zh: 这个城市真的必须在公众教育和争取认同上下足功夫，这样在这个新的执法机构中就不需要那种权力和武力了。

sentences.en: So I think if the public understands the direct connection between their cooperation with traffic agents and society's reliance on policing,
sentences.zh: 所以我想，如果公众理解了他们对交通协管员的配合与社会对警务的依赖之间的直接联系，

sentences.en: then that could go a long way towards not having to fall back into the cycle of increasing the discretionary authority of whoever it is that enforces traffic laws.
sentences.zh: 那么这将在很大程度上避免让我们重新陷入扩大任何交通执法人员自由裁量权的恶性循环。

sentences.en: So it's the really early stages of all this, but I think it's really exciting that people are trying to shake things up and try new things.
sentences.zh: 所以这一切还处于非常初期的阶段，但我认为人们敢于打破常规、尝试新鲜事物，这真的很令人兴奋。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And interesting.
sentences.zh: 而且很有趣。

sentences.en: I mean, it's cool for me to see Berkeley sort of at the center of all this history going back 100 years and now coming full circle.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，看到伯克利成为这一切历史的中心，回溯100年，现在又兜了一个圈子回到原点，这对我来说很酷。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's like it's almost poetic that it's happening here when it all kind of started here.
sentences.zh: 这就好像是一种诗意的巧合，一切都在这里开始，现在又在这里发生。

sentences.en: So this is so cool.
sentences.zh: 这太酷了。

sentences.en: Well, thanks so much for for for bringing this in and having this to the interview.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你把这个带到节目中来并接受采访。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: Yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 不客气。
